summary: A zero-based budget you own: accounts and categories, a monthly grid where every dollar is assigned, a To Be Budgeted figure that turns red when you over-assign, CSV import with remembered column mappings and payee rules, reconciliation against the real bank balance, credit cards handled the way a budget should, and optional bank sync through SimpleFIN for about $15 a year instead of YNAB's price.

stack.why: many views and forms; the framework earns its place
a budget that disagrees with the bank by a cent loses all trust
a transaction happens on a date; timezone shifts move money between months
this is your money; it does not need to be on the internet

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A CSV export from each bank account
prerequisites.why: Phase 4 imports real data; you need a file per account to test column mapping and sign conventions.
prerequisites.get: In your bank's web app, find Export or Download transactions, choose CSV, last 90 days. Save one per account, including a credit card.

prerequisites.name: Your category groups and categories, written down
prerequisites.why: The budget grid is built on them. Deciding in a spreadsheet first stops Phase 2 from becoming a planning session.
prerequisites.get: Groups like Bills, Everyday, Savings Goals; six to fifteen categories total to start.

prerequisites.name: Today's real balance for every account
prerequisites.why: Reconciliation in Phase 5 needs the true figure.
prerequisites.get: Read them off the bank apps now and note the date.

prerequisites.name: A SimpleFIN Bridge access token (optional)
prerequisites.why: Automatic bank sync, the one thing CSV import cannot replace. About $15 a year, and what Actual Budget uses for the same job. You never hold bank credentials; the aggregator does.
prerequisites.get: beta-bridge.simplefin.org > sign up > connect your banks > create an access token (a setup token you exchange once for an access URL). Put the access URL in .env.

env.name: DATE_FORMAT_HINT
env.where: Your bank's CSV date format, asked once per account on import and stored.

env.name: SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL
env.where: From SimpleFIN after exchanging the setup token. Empty disables sync.

phases.title: Accounts and transactions
phases.goal: Fast keyboard entry, balances computed by query, cents stored exactly.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: accounts (id, name, kind, on_budget, closed), category_groups, categories, budgets (month, category_id, assigned_cents), transactions (id, account_id, date, payee, category_id, amount_cents signed, memo, cleared, reconciled, transfer_transaction_id), payee_rules.
commands: mkdir budget && cd budget && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Build account CRUD and the transaction entry form
steps.detail: Keyboard-first: date, payee, category, amount, memo, enter to save. Parse 12.10 into 1210; never store a float.

steps.do: Compute balances by query, not stored
steps.detail: A cached balance drifts and you cannot tell which number lies.

check: Ten transactions across two accounts yield balances matching a hand sum
Editing an amount updates the balance; deleting restores it
Entering 12.10 stores 1210 and renders $12.10 exactly

phases.title: Categories and the budget grid
phases.goal: Assigned, activity and available per category per month, with rollover.

steps.do: Build groups and categories from your list
Build the monthly grid
steps.detail: activity = sum of the category's transactions that month; available = last month's available + assigned + activity.

check: Assign $200 to Groceries, spend $50: assigned 200, activity -50, available 150
Next month opens with 150 available before anything is assigned
An overspent -20 carries into the next month rather than resetting

phases.title: To Be Budgeted
phases.goal: The header number the whole method rests on.

steps.do: Compute inflow to on-budget accounts minus everything assigned across all months
steps.detail: One query; reconcile it against a hand calculation on a fixture.

steps.do: Show it in the header on every budget page, red when negative
steps.detail: This number is the entire method: every dollar has a job, and the app's job is to tell you when one does not.

check: Adding $1,000 income raises it by exactly 1000
Assigning $400 lowers it by 400
Over-assigning turns it red with the correct negative figure

phases.title: CSV import
phases.goal: Import any bank's CSV once you have mapped it, dedupe, and learn payees.

steps.do: Build the column-mapping step per account
steps.detail: Date, payee, amount or debit/credit columns. Ask the date format once and store it; never guess between DD/MM and MM/DD.

steps.do: Dedupe on date, amount and payee and preview what will be skipped
Apply payee_rules and learn a rule when you categorize a new payee

check: Importing the same file twice adds nothing the second time
An ambiguous date format is asked about rather than assumed
A credit-card CSV with inverted signs imports with correct polarity
A known payee arrives pre-categorized

phases.title: Reconciliation
phases.goal: Match the bank to the cent and lock what matched.

steps.do: Build the reconcile flow
steps.detail: Enter the real balance, see the difference against cleared, tick transactions cleared until zero, lock them reconciled.

steps.do: Offer a balance adjustment transaction for a remaining difference
steps.detail: An auditable row rather than a silent edit of history.

check: A $3 discrepancy is reported precisely
Ticking the missing transaction clears it
Reconciled transactions resist accidental edits
The adjustment path leaves an auditable row

phases.title: Credit cards
phases.goal: Spending on a card moves the assigned money to the card's payment category.

steps.do: Implement the credit-card payment category rule
steps.detail: A categorized purchase on a card reduces that category's available and raises the card's payment category by the same amount.

steps.do: Treat paying the card as a transfer that reduces both
steps.detail: Show the payment category in the grid so the money set aside for the bill is visible.

check: A $50 grocery purchase on a card reduces Groceries by 50 and raises the card payment category by 50
Paying the card as a transfer reduces both correctly

phases.title: Reports and backups
phases.goal: Spending by category and net worth, and a backup you have restored.

steps.do: Build the two reports as inline SVG
Nightly copy of the database to backups/, thirty kept, and one restore performed

check: Report totals match the transaction table
A restore has been performed once

phases.title: Optional bank sync, honestly priced
phases.goal: SimpleFIN behind an interface, with CSV as the other implementation and no bank credentials in your app.

steps.do: Exchange the setup token for the access URL once
commands: curl -s $(echo $SETUP_TOKEN | base64 -d)  # the decoded setup token is a claim URL; POST to it once to receive the access URL

steps.do: Implement the sync source
steps.detail: GET the access URL's /accounts, map transactions to your model, dedupe against manual entries by date, amount and payee.

check: A sync pulls new transactions and dedupes against manual entries
The app works completely with sync disabled and no token present

phases.title: Run it on a server for two people
phases.goal: Only if you share the budget: HTTPS, a login, off-box backups.

steps.do: Add a single-user login and bind behind Caddy with HTTPS
Nightly off-box encrypted backup with age
Uptime check and structured logs

check: The login is required for every route
A restore from the encrypted backup opens correctly

product.outcome: A budget two people can share with confidence: exact money maths, imports that never double, a bank sync you chose knowingly, backups encrypted off the box.

architecture.swap: The core; everything else reads it

architecture.owns: CSV mapping, dedupe, payee rules, and the SimpleFIN source
architecture.swap: Add another aggregator as a second source

operations.backup: Nightly SQLite backup, encrypted with age when off the box.
operations.restore: Decrypt, copy back, open; check TBB matches the last known figure.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz when hosted; a failed sync is shown in the UI.
operations.incident: If the SimpleFIN URL leaks, revoke it in SimpleFIN and issue a new token; your app never held bank passwords.

releaseGate: Money maths verified against a hand-built month
Import dedupe verified on a real bank file twice

notIncluded: Mobile apps and family sharing beyond two logins.
The educational method and habit design, which is a real part of what YNAB sells.
after: Goals per category (save X by month Y) shown in the grid
A PWA shell so the phone can add a transaction
